objective: Make Craft spending reveal material technologies and repeatable buyables, while retaining manual Water hauling alongside a smaller spring and meaningful storage/pipe choices.

include: Three initial rows: Crafting 10 Craft, Clay 20 Craft, recommended Copper working 30 Craft; each has one unlock tile and four related purchases
Craft-based buyable access, prerequisite migration and resolved hut bootstrap
Manual plus passive Water, eight-person baseline, communal cistern and fired-clay pipes
Save/prestige preservation, truthful UI and legal balance coverage
exclude: Production implementation in this planning task
New raw-material stockpiles or harvesting loops; Bronze/Iron rows remain future suggestions
New fishing discovery, farming/automation redesign, weather or water-quality simulation
Native milestone enrollment, acceptance, merges, deployment and service activation

acceptance_criteria: MAT01-AC01: Each row has exactly five tiles: one capability purchase at 10/20/30 Craft followed by four purchases at 1/2/3 Craft respectively; the 30-Craft Copper row is the requested architect recommendation.
MAT01-AC02: The first successful row-unlock purchase permanently reveals its four related tiles. Failed, repeated one-time or insufficient-funds purchases spend nothing and reveal nothing.

MAT01-AC03: Craft capability predicates replace the Organization-6 buyable gate and bigger-game per-level Organization requirement. Organization retention, automation and unrelated activity gates remain explicit; bootstrap follows the resolved D2 decision.
MAT01-AC04: Every listed upgrade and repeatable project has an observable effect, truthful cost and shared simulation/UI eligibility; direct locked commands reject atomically.
MAT01-AC05: Collect water remains visible and dispatchable with a spring, including after reload, with normal worker/full-storage/busy guards and active snapshots.

MAT01-AC06: A spring without Water improvements supports exactly eight current-upkeep equivalents: zero net Water at eight and negative at nine, including Organization balance changes. This is sustainable supply, not a Population cap.

MAT01-AC07: Communal cistern costs 2 Craft and adds 200 capacity without adding stock/income or changing Emergency cistern. Fired-clay pipes spend 2 Craft plus exactly 2 Fire once and multiply only spring flow by exactly 2.

MAT01-AC08: Material knowledge, owned row upgrades and cistern/pipes survive both prestiges. Repeatable projects retain/reset by exact IDs; new water baskets use the explicit Organization-4 Water-storage retention extension.

MAT01-AC09: Supported old Civ exports migrate atomically to the one current schema, preserving currencies, bought effects, active jobs, paid construction and applicable retention. Malformed imports preserve live and durable state; ptr stays untouched.

MAT01-AC10: A legal fresh-game policy reaches the first material and each later row without resource grants or an unlock cycle. Active and regular balance runs report observed cost/time, cadence and completion or stalls; rough/fixed comparisons cover the new sections.

MAT01-AC11: Desktop/narrow keyboard journeys cover row purchase, revealed upgrades, affordability, manual hauling after spring, cistern filling and pipe purchase/depletion rejection; no stale unlock or double charge after save replacement.

MAT01-AC12: Focused rules/save/balance/browser checks and full npm test pass on the implementation candidate; canonical design, developer map and progression text match shipped behavior. Planning validation alone cannot satisfy these criteria.
constraints: Planning-only authorization; proposed tuning values are not recorded as owner answers
One canonical civilization rules owner, one save model/runtime, session-bound state and normal codec ingress
Preserve branch writers, old save recovery, upstream attribution and all unrelated Organization rewards
Resolve the remaining hut-bootstrap decision D2 and validate exact-file preparation before any separately authorized implementation

decisions.question: Which stages are authorized?
decisions.answer: Produce an implementation plan and branch off the latest work.
decisions.evidence_reference: Current user request beginning Implementation plan

decisions.question: What Water behavior is required?
decisions.answer: Keep manual hauling after spring; reduce baseline automatic supply to support 8 Population; add large cistern storage and 2-Fire pipes giving 2x automatic Water.

decisions.question: What do materials represent?
decisions.answer: Permanent capability row unlocks in Craft without harvested material balances. Four related purchases follow each unlock; basket buyables use actual repeatable construction.
decisions.rationale: Uses existing Craft currency and improvement/project owners; avoids adding an unrequested collection economy.
decisions.evidence_reference: Current request first buy unlocks material; civilization.js improvements and projects

decisions.question: How is eight-person support measured?
decisions.answer: Use shared actual upkeep u: spring flow = u * (8 + wellLevel) * knowledgeEffect * (pipes ? 2 : 1). Zero flow without spring. Remove the old 24 + 10*wellLevel formula.
decisions.rationale: Organization already reduces demand. Sharing u keeps the unmodified baseline exactly eight sustainable people even after Organization spending.
decisions.evidence_reference: civilization.js waterFlow and supply; user eight-population baseline

decisions.question: What is the intended row structure?
decisions.answer: Five tiles total per row: Crafting 10 Craft then four purchases at 1 Craft; Clay 20 Craft then four at 2 Craft. Thatched roofs, Wooden spears and Woven baskets belong in the first row.
decisions.evidence_reference: User correction beginning No: Crafting (10 craft). then 4 more buyables for 1 craft each.

decisions.question: Which fourth basic purchase?
decisions.answer: Digging sticks, with the existing +25% Gather effect.
decisions.rationale: The owner requested one researched additional basic upgrade. It gives gathering a distinct benefit and reuses an existing rule.
decisions.evidence_reference: Owner correction; hash-verified Plant part 1 paragraphs 61-64; existing digging improvement

decisions.question: Which technology fits 30 Craft?
decisions.answer: Recommend Copper working at 30 Craft with four 3-Craft tool purchases. Suggest Bronze working at 50 Craft later, outside this initial table.
decisions.rationale: The owner explicitly asked the agent to choose. Copper offers a separate first-metal tier; bronze introduces alloying, commonly copper with tin. This is a game progression recommendation, not a universal historical sequence.
decisions.evidence_reference: Owner phrase 30 craft - bronze? You tell me; Ashmolean Bronze Age collection; Tel Tsaf excavation; Met copper-alloy chisel

decisions.question: How do the corrected costs apply?
decisions.answer: Unlock 10/20/30 Craft; four related purchases per row at 1/2/3 Craft. Jars technology is repriced to 2 Craft as requested. Pipes additionally spend 2 Fire; existing jar-construction firing costs remain.
decisions.rationale: Applies the explicit correction while preserving the earlier pipe Fire requirement and existing paid construction. No extra upfront Fire charge is added to the jars technology.
decisions.evidence_reference: Owner correction and original Water paragraph; current Fire-branch jar construction

open_questions.question: How should huts bootstrap buyables that move to the Crafting row?
options: Keep labor-only huts at Organization 1; move other buyables to Craft capabilities
Move huts too; make the first Craft reachable at 8 Population and add a 1-Craft starter hut capability outside material rows
open_questions.recommended_default: Keep labor-only huts at Organization 1; move other buyables to Craft capabilities
open_questions.consequence: Current housing caps at 8 and Craft starts at 12. Requiring the 10-Craft Crafting tile for all hut construction would deadlock. Moving huts needs an explicit Craft-economy amendment before implementation.
open_questions.evidence_reference: Current chat asynchronous hut-scope question; civilization.js startingSettlement, housing defaults, prestigeGain and featureAvailable
